# MM-P3-L1-SB02 - Maintenance manual - Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-SB02

Scope
This manual covers planned preventive maintenance and in-service inspection activities for the Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02). It is intended for use by qualified maintenance technicians and shift engineers. The document includes background and rationale for tasks, required tools, stepwise procedures written for clarity, and acceptance criteria for completed work. Use this manual in conjunction with related documentation: MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3, SB-1027, and SOP-P3-L1-04.

Background and rationale
The shot blast cabinet provides surface conditioning of hot-forged parts prior to downstream operations. Regular maintenance is required to preserve blast efficiency, prevent component damage, and limit downtime. Wear on the blast wheel liner affects pattern distribution and media containment; incorrect clamping or loose fasteners accelerates wear and increases risk of foreign object ingress. Maintaining the shot media inventory within specified levels ensures consistent abrasive exposure and avoids impact energy drift. The specified bolt torque and media top-up interval are based on manufacturer recommendations and plant validation to provide repeatable, safe operation.

Tools
- Torque wrench set suitable for 65 N·m
- Socket to suit blast wheel liner bolts
- Portable vacuum suited for abrasive media recovery
- Replacement wear liners as specified in MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3
- Media sampling container and visual comparator as detailed in SB-1027
- Personal protective equipment per SOP-P3-L1-04

Procedure
Pre-maintenance checks and preparations
- Confirm lockout/tagout and energy isolation per SOP-P3-L1-04. Verify isolation before any access to the cabinet interior.
- Notify operations and log planned work in the maintenance schedule system referenced by MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3. Record the equipment id EQ-P3-L1-SB02 on all entries.
- Inspect the cabinet exterior for signs of leaking seals or fastener damage that may indicate internal issues.

Blast wheel liner inspection and replacement
- Remove access panels to expose the blast wheel and liner area. Clean loose media and dust with a portable vacuum to allow clear visual inspection.
- Visually inspect the liner for cracking, deformation, or local thinning. Refer to MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3 for liner part selection and fitment orientation.
- If liner replacement is required, loosen bolts sufficiently to remove the liner. When reinstalling or securing a liner, apply the blast wheel liner bolt torque for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 65 N·m. Use a calibrated torque wrench and follow the star pattern described in MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3 to ensure uniform clamp load.
- Rationale: consistent bolt torque prevents vibration-driven loosening and minimizes differential wear between liner segments.

Shot media management
- Prior to media sampling, isolate the media hopper and ensure dust extraction is operational. Draw a representative sample and compare against the visual comparator protocol in SB-1027 to determine contamination level and shot size degradation.
- When the sample indicates need for top-up, add shot media to the hopper until normal operating level is restored. The shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 45 hours. Record each top-up action in the media log.
- Rationale: regular top-ups at the specified interval maintain consistent abrasive mass flow and mitigate overloading of separation systems.

Wear monitoring and auxiliary components
- Inspect separator screens, dust collector connections, and feed gates for accumulation and wear. Clear obstructions and replace components per MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3 where visible degradation is present.
- Check feed rates and observe blast pattern with a test panel (use a known reference part) to confirm efficacy after maintenance. Record observations and attach photos to the work order.

Safety and housekeeping
- Remove debris and ensure that all guards and access panels are reinstated. Confirm torque values on critical fasteners and enter readings in the maintenance log.
- Perform a functional run in single-cycle mode as permitted by SOP-P3-L1-04 to verify normal operation before returning the cabinet to production.

Examples and notes
- Example record entry: equipment EQ-P3-L1-SB02; activity: liner torque check; bolt torque applied: 65 N·m; media top-up performed: yes; media interval observed: 45 hours; inspector: technician name; attached photos: yes. Use MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3 forms for part references and SB-1027 for media analysis.
- If recurring loosening of liner bolts is observed despite correct torque application, escalate to engineering and reference SB-1027 for contamination-related causes. Document any deviation from the normal procedure and the corrective action taken.

Records to keep
- Maintenance work order including date, technician name, and equipment id EQ-P3-L1-SB02.
- Torque readings and tool calibration reference for the torque wrench used.
- Media sampling results and comparator records as per SB-1027.
- Media top-up log entries showing that the shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 45 hours was adhered to.
- Replacement liner part traceability and installation records per MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3.

Acceptance criteria
- All blast wheel liner bolts are torqued to the specified blast wheel liner bolt torque for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 65 N·m; torque readings entered and tool calibration confirmed.
- Visual inspection confirms liners are free of cracking and within acceptable wear limits defined in MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3.
- Media sample meets acceptance per SB-1027 or corrective actions are recorded and executed.
- Media top-up activity and interval are recorded, demonstrating compliance with the shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 45 hours.
- Functional test run demonstrates normal blast pattern and no abnormal vibrations or leaks. Any deviation must be documented and corrected before returning to production.

References
- MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3
- SB-1027
- SOP-P3-L1-04
